observations: The site header and section navigation wrap a 720px settings content column. Sections switch to a horizontal tab bar at or below 720px, with inline loading and retry states.
inferences: My weekly report can follow this section layout and use the existing Card, Field, Button and Input patterns.
limitations: The settings layout does not currently establish the proposed subscription flow or its access rules.

observations: The neutral shell, Radix colors, typography, hairline borders, restrained radii and field rows are reflected in apps/dashboard/src/lib/styles/tokens.css, radix.css and the Svelte UI components.
limitations: The standalone HTML uses a token subset and system font fallbacks. It reproduces the relevant patterns without including the application shell runtime.

observations: The viewer role has no existing settings section. SiteHeader.svelte links to the first visible section. The organization editor sees block rules, goals, and sharing.
inferences: A new personal section gives an authorized viewer a Settings tab without granting the viewer access to other sections.
limitations: The prototype runs without a session or network. It illustrates the intended UI access boundary only.

observations: Status is off, pending or active; a pending code lasts 15 minutes and is a 43-character base64url token. One request per account per minute across sites (429). The fifth wrong code clears the pending code. Wrong, expired and cleared codes all return 400 invalid_code. Request returns 503 mail_unavailable without SMTP and 502 mail_failed after storing the new code when SMTP refuses it.

Reports cover the previous complete site-local week and are sent after 09:00 on the site's first weekday. The body carries the site name, ISO from/to dates, time zone, visitors, visits, pageviews, {base}/s/{site_id} and a last line Unsubscribe: {base}/api/weekly-report/unsubscribe/{token} (Chinese 退订周报：). {base} is RIVU_BASE_URL without trailing slashes. Subjects are fixed per language.

Each claimed send record gets a new 43-character base64url token; only its SHA-256 hash is stored with the user, the site and the confirmation time of the subscription. GET /api/weekly-report/unsubscribe/{token} returns a confirmation page and changes nothing; POST turns the subscription off (clears the email and the confirmation) while the confirmation time still matches, and otherwise returns the expired-or-already-off page. A malformed token is 404. The pages are fixed bilingual HTML, no cookie or session, with Content-Security-Policy default-src 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none', plus no-store and no-referrer.
inferences: The settings page can only show one message for an invalid code and must re-read status to learn that a code was voided.
limitations: The API does not return the stored email language, the next send date or the confirmation time.
The unsubscribe pages ignore the email language and the CSP rules out styles, scripts and images, so they stay unstyled unless the response policy changes.
The settings page and the HTML email do not exist in production; the API, the plain-text emails and the unsubscribe pages do.

observations: remove_member deletes the member's weekly report subscriptions for the organization's sites unless a site guest membership remains. remove_guest deletes the guest's subscription for that site unless an organization membership remains. Send records are kept.
inferences: A user who lost access sees the unavailable-site message, and a subscription from before the loss does not come back with the access.
limitations: A disabled or deleted account is not cleaned up by these two functions; the sender skips such accounts when it picks recipients.

observations: Mailer::send builds a single text/plain message in Mailer::message. When Mail.unsubscribe_url is set (weekly reports only) the message gets a List-Unsubscribe: <url> header. Invitation and password reset emails use the same plain-text style without it.
inferences: An HTML email needs a multipart/alternative change in Mailer::message; the List-Unsubscribe header can stay as it is.
limitations: There is no List-Unsubscribe-Post header, so one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) is not implemented.

observations: The primary variant uses --accent-solid with --accent-contrast text.
